titleEn: Even in the Dark, I Hear Breathing!

pages.text: "Don't put out the lamp!" Yuki pulled the quilt to their chin. Grandma covered the brazier with ashes and held the lamp. Brown dog Momo curled in a corner.
Grandma blew it out. The room was dark. "I'm scared. Light it again, please." Yuki covered their nose with the quilt and squeezed their eyes shut.
Something pointed appeared against the paper door. Yuki pulled the quilt over their head. "What is that...?" Sniffling came from underneath.
Grandma lifted the quilt slightly and held Yuki's hand. She lit a small lamp again. "What looked so pointed? Show me."
Yuki pointed to the paper door. "There. The pointed thing." Grandma took the lamp to it. "Let's see together what it is."
She slid the paper door open. Icicles hung in rows from the eaves. "Wow, the pointed things were icicles!" Yuki's eyes widened.
Grandma blew out the lamp. The room grew dark again. But beside Yuki came breathing in and out. A hand reached onto Momo's rising and falling back. "Even in the Dark, I Hear Breathing!"
Listening, Yuki heard Grandma's breathing, too. In and out. Three breathing sounds filled the dark room. "It wasn't empty after all." Yuki was no longer scared.

The next night, Yuki untied the scarf and set it by their head. When the lamp went out, Yuki uncovered their ears. "One, say aloud that I'm scared! Two, take a lamp and see what it is! Three, listen to breathing!"

Grandma pulled the quilt to Yuki's shoulders and patted their back. "Even when the light goes out, the place beside you stays the same." Yuki rested a hand on Momo's back. "Even in the Dark, I Hear Breathing!"
